stages.title: Search planning
instructions: Write strict JSON matching {"version":1,"topic":"...","query_variants":[...],"taxonomy_cells":[{"cell":"...","query_variants":["...","...","..."]}],"exclusion_terms":[],"venue_priorities":[],"source_types":[...]}. Preserve every project taxonomy coverage cell verbatim as a taxonomy_cells[].cell; each cell must have at least 3 distinct query variants.
Cover method families, evaluation/benchmark terms, prior surveys, and application variants. Prefer queries that can retrieve both recent and foundational work.

stages.title: Outline
instructions: When feedback/outline-revision.md is present, treat it as the human's requested changes for this outline revision. Implement it while preserving the evidence-first scope and emit matching outline.md and outline.json.

Every outline.json section MUST include: id, title, role, target_words, purpose, keywords (at least two strings), and source_ids. keywords are the retrieval terms used for its section evidence packet.

For a survey contract, assign exactly these role values where applicable: introduction_gap_contributions, multi_axis_taxonomy, method_family (at least two sections), related_work_differentiation, limitations_future_work, or body. Include each required role at least once, and use body only for remaining sections.

stages.title: Plan placed figures and tables
instructions: Write strict JSON with version:1 and placements:[{id,placement:{section_id,discussion}}]. Select no artifact unless it makes a specific argument easier to understand. You—not a preset menu—choose the reader question, visual form, placement, and supporting sources. A legacy concept_map remains supported, but prefer diagrams:[{id,title,caption,insight,placement:{section_id,discussion},source_ids:[existing classified source ids],nodes:[{id,label}],edges:[{from,to,label?}]}] for any explanatory relationship: a taxonomy, mechanism, causal/control loop, process, trade-off, or argument map. Each diagram needs 3--10 short nodes and only relationships supported by its cited corpus. Add concept-illustration only when it is explicitly selected, the optional Nano Banana backend is enabled, and it provides orientation rather than evidence. Never select corpus bookkeeping, source inventories, DOI/venue listings, or a decorative chart.

The same JSON also supports a declarative figure-spec contract: timelines:[{id,title,caption,insight,placement:{section_id,discussion},source_ids:[three or more existing classified source ids]}] and table_specs:[{id,kind:<agent-chosen reader purpose>,comparative?:true|false,title,caption,insight,placement:{section_id,discussion},headers:[2--6 labels],rows:[{cells:[one per header],source_ids:[one or more existing classified source ids]}]}]. The agent chooses whether a timeline, table, diagram, verified numeric plot, imported empirical figure, or no artifact best serves the paper. Timelines derive dates and coordinates from verified metadata; table_specs derive the generated CSV, Markdown, longtable TeX, caption, label, and placement from this contract. Never supply raw TeX, plot code, arbitrary numbers, unsupported ratings, or unknown source ids. Every artifact you select needs an insight stating why a reader needs it; a legacy concept_map takes insight too, and a verified metadata plot takes its framing from metadata_plots:[{metric:publication_year|citation_depth|venue,insight,title?,caption?}]. An artifact with no insight fails the release gate rather than borrowing a generic one.
Place each artifact in the section whose argument it supports. Do not create an appendix-style generated-artifacts section.

Follow the injected project brief for audience, target length, and style. Do not cite a URL/file directly from the brief: recognized scholarly links enter through authoritative reference seeds and may be cited only after they appear in the section evidence packet; all other links/files remain contextual leads. Cite factual claims only with exact packet chunk ids.

Write complete reader-facing prose for this section, aiming for its outline.json target_words allocation. Do not emit a scaffold, source inventory, or a shorter placeholder merely because later revision exists.

Do not emit Markdown pipe tables, hand-numbered Table/Figure references, or prose pretending to be a diagram. The artifact builder owns captions, labels, table layout, and rendered figures; explain the comparison or relationship in prose and let the placed artifact carry the formal reference.

Use inline `$...$` or display `$$...$$` notation when it clarifies a sourced definition, objective, comparison, or analytical claim. Define every symbol in nearby prose and cite the supporting packet immediately before or after it. A literature-derived equation must be attributed; an author-created formalization must be labelled as a definition, model, or illustrative bound with its assumptions and must not be called a theorem, result, or empirical finding. Never add decorative equations or imply an experiment not supported by the evidence packet.
For research prose, cite only exact chunk ids from the injected evidence packet: [source:<source-id>:p<paragraph>]. A generic [source:<source-id>] marker is not enough for publication validation.
Do not cite a source merely because it appears in source_ids. If no packet chunk supports a factual claim, remove or qualify the claim.

stages.title: Write research-paper abstract
instructions: Write paper/abstract.md as 150--250 words of reader-facing survey prose: the research problem, scope and selection basis, organizing contribution, main synthesis, and principal limitation or open question. Do not mention LongWrite, agents, prompts, or workflow mechanics. Do not use citations, source markers, headings other than an optional '# Abstract', or unsupported claims.

stages.title: Render caption-bearing PDF pages for multimodal visual review
stages.disabled_reason: seed/dry-run rehearsal cannot attach rendered page images to a multimodal reviewer

stages.title: Inspect rendered figures and tables for reader-facing legibility
instructions: Inspect the attached PNG pages as visual input, not merely their filenames or PDF text. Check every rendered page for overlapping labels/arrows/nodes, clipping, illegibly small text, unsafe contrast, table overflow/truncation, misplaced captions, and visual claims that the reader cannot verify.

Write reviews/visual-qa.json as strict JSON: {version:1,render_manifest_sha256:<sha256 of reports/visual-render-manifest.json including its trailing newline>,status:pass|fail,inspected_pages:[every rendered page number],observations:[{page,observation}],findings:[{id,severity:minor|major|critical,page,summary,remediation}],summary}. Every page needs a concrete observation. status: pass is legal only with no major/critical finding; status: fail requires at least one major/critical finding.
This is a visual QA record, not a prose review. Do not edit figures, TeX, or manuscript text. A major or critical defect must name the page and an actionable renderer/placement repair.
Also write reviews/visual-qa.md as a concise reader-facing summary of the observations and findings.

stages.title: Baseline simulated peer review
instructions: Treat every metadata-only or missing-evidence citation in reports/evidence-audit.md as a major review finding. Do not reward prose whose factual claims are not backed by exact evidence-packet chunk citations.

Review the rendered PDF hierarchy, placed figures, placed tables, captions, and in-text references. A file path or literal [source:...] marker printed in the manuscript is a blocking artifact defect, not a figure, table, or reader-facing citation.

Reward a well-designed explanatory diagram, source-grounded timeline, or qualitative comparison matrix when it makes the manuscript's argument more legible than prose. Review these for a clear analytical takeaway, source grounding, readable labels, and non-redundancy. For every equation, verify nearby symbol definitions and a literature citation or an explicit author-formalization label with stated assumptions; treat an unsupported theorem, conjecture, quantitative chart, or percentage as a major finding. Judge under-use as well as over-use: where a section argues a comparison across several sources in prose that a reader would follow far more easily as a table or diagram, say so and name the sections and the axis being compared. Do not ask for an artifact merely to raise a count, and never for one the cited evidence cannot support.
Treat a failing reviews/visual-qa.json as an independently verified major/critical artifact finding. Do not award a high review score while its page-specific legibility defects remain unresolved.

Use the injected project brief and outline.json as the length contract. Treat a manuscript materially below its total target or a section materially below its target_words as a release-blocking finding; name the sections and the evidence-grounded expansion needed, never recommend filler.
When feedback/user-feedback.md is present, evaluate the manuscript against the operator's requests as well as the evidence and release criteria. Make each unresolved request explicit in the review.

stages.title: Decide whether this round must change the frame
Record the artifact directions this loop has already tried
Report where validated evidence sits and what the visual plan serves
Choose source-grounded analytical artifacts
instructions: Read the review evidence and decide whether an additional analytical artifact would materially improve this paper. Write ONLY reviews/artifact-plan.json; use an empty intents array when no artifact is justified. Never use a count target to justify pipeline telemetry, source inventories, venue/DOI lists, packet-status fields, full-title lists, or decorative charts.

reports/comparison-opportunities.md lists, per outline section, the sources carrying validated evidence packets, the taxonomy cells they span, the limitations they record, the comparison dimensions their claims name verbatim, and which artifacts the manuscript already carries there. Read it before deciding. A section holding several packet-backed sources across multiple taxonomy cells with no artifact is where a comparison is most likely to earn its place; a section already served needs no second artifact. It is an observation, never a target: there is no correct number of artifacts, a section may be better served by prose, and an artifact the listed evidence does not support is exactly the failure this report exists to prevent. Judge the dimensions yourself — they are free text, so two sources can name the same axis in different words, and only some of them are worth a table.

The current artifact-plan contract additionally permits timeline and architecture_diagram intents. A timeline needs a target section and at least three classified source IDs; an architecture diagram follows this profile's requirement: An architecture_diagram requires a target section and at least 3 classified scholarly source IDs. The visual renderer derives dates from metadata and never accepts handwritten coordinates or result values.

Schema: {version:1,intents:[{id,kind,rationale,section_id?,source_ids?,taxonomy_cell?,plot_metric?,experiment_hypothesis?,control?,acceptance_criteria:[{metric,target,scope?}]}]}. kind is formalization, comparison_matrix, metadata_plot, timeline, architecture_diagram, taxonomy_recall, or empirical_pilot.

Formalization is a request for the chapter writer to introduce a compact definition/objective with locally defined symbols; it requires a target section and supporting classified source ids. Do not request decorative mathematics.

comparison_matrix requires representative source ids. metadata_plot must select publication_year, citation_depth, or venue and a target section; its renderer derives values only from verified workspace metadata. timeline requires a target section and at least three classified source ids; its renderer derives dates and labels only from verified workspace metadata. An architecture_diagram requires a target section and at least 3 classified scholarly source IDs. taxonomy_recall must name one configured taxonomy cell and target woven A/B evidence.

empirical_pilot is legal only when research.paper_kind is empirical. It must state a hypothesis, control, and trial acceptance criterion. It creates a preregistration request only; LongWrite does not execute an experiment until the configured LongExperiment integration is available.
Choose at most five intents. Do not invent source ids, sections, taxonomy cells, commands, experimental results, or plot values.

stages.title: Plan bounded remediation actions
instructions: Read the review evidence and write ONLY reviews/action-plan.json. Do not wrap it in Markdown or an array.

reports/stall-status.md decides which tools are eligible this round, from recorded scores rather than from your own judgment of progress. When its posture is `structural`, several rounds have already failed to beat the best score, and every action you emit must use a tool it lists as eligible — repeating prose or visual revision would run a shape that has demonstrably not worked. Pivot the structure, not the tactics: change the outline's frame or the evidence the paper rests on. When the posture is `escalate`, say so plainly in the findings: the binding constraint is likely outside what this loop can change.

reviews/artifact-plan.json is the validated creative strategy. Route every selected intent to the smallest compatible action; do not discard a validated formalization, comparison, metadata plot, timeline, architecture diagram, or taxonomy recall merely because it is not a fixed stage.

Schema: {version:1,findings:[{id,severity,summary}],actions:[{id,tool,finding_ids,rationale,acceptance_criteria:[{metric,target,scope?}]}]}. severity is minor, major, or critical. Every action needs at least one measurable criterion. Use cited_sources, cited_within_one_year_ratio, accepted_cited_ratio, cited_arxiv_only_ratio, citations_per_page, citation_depth_per_section (scope=A|B|C or a named section), taxonomy_cell_ab_sources (scope=taxonomy cell), comparative_tables, verified_metadata_plots, figures, tables, rendered_visual_review, or empirical_trials. Map weak comparative synthesis to a source-grounded method matrix; map taxonomy gaps to targeted recall plus woven A/B sources; map visual weakness to rendered_visual_review >= 1 plus the smallest necessary figure/table repair. Never use an empirical_trials action unless research.paper_kind is empirical and a preregistered, controlled result artifact is in scope.

Allowed tools: targeted_research_expansion (only for an evidence/coverage gap), reopen_outline (only for a major/critical structural, scope, or taxonomy defect requiring a changed organizing argument), revise_sections (for prose, structure, citation, or length repair), revise_visual_plan (for a figure/table placement, caption, conceptual-diagram, generated-table, bibliography-presentation, or rendered-PDF defect), and request_operator_clarification (only when a human decision is genuinely required).

Select reopen_outline only when incremental chapter revision cannot address the review finding. Its rationale must name the defective organizing claim and evidence-backed replacement. It may co-occur with targeted_research_expansion: the dispatcher refreshes and validates the literature before it reopens the outline in the same bounded round.

Output ownership is strict: revise_sections may change only chapters/*.md, paper/abstract.md, and reviews/revision-report.md. Never assign it a generated table/figure, placement, caption, rendered-PDF, bibliography-presentation, TeX, or build defect. Assign those findings to revise_visual_plan so the artifact builder can write the durable placement contract before the normal rebuild.

If one finding spans prose and an artifact, split it into two findings (or attach the same finding id to both actions) and keep each action rationale within that action's declared outputs. Do not ask a prose action to hand off uneditable work as a blocker.
Select each tool at most once per plan. Combine all findings owned by the same tool into that tool's single action; its output contract is shared across those findings.
Every action must name at least one finding id and at least one quantitative acceptance criterion. Select the smallest sufficient set; do not invent commands, paths, tool ids, or model settings.
If a finding requires an operator decision, select request_operator_clarification as the ONLY action. Put the exact question in its rationale; never guess the answer.

stages.title: Order remediation actions by evidence dependency
Execute structural outline-reopen actions after evidence refresh
Execute prose and visual repair actions from refreshed evidence
Double-review citation-backed sampled claims
instructions: Deterministically sample substantive cited claims from every section. Use stable sample ids like claim-001.

Write reviews/claim-judgments.jsonl with TWO independent JSONL judgments per sample_id, reviewer_id values reviewer_a and reviewer_b, and fields {sample_id,reviewer_id,source_id,chapter,claim,evidence_locators,prompt_hash,model,runtime,verdict,rationale}. verdict must be entailed, partial, or unsupported.
Judge the exact evidence packet/chunk locators, not source metadata. Any disagreement must be routed to human review or revision before release.

tool_catalog.title: Expand research evidence for an identified coverage gap
Reopen the approved outline for a structural correction
instructions: This action is authorized only because the validated plan selected reopen_outline. Rewrite outline.md and outline.json to repair the named major/critical structural, scope, or taxonomy defect. Use only current classified source IDs and contributions backed by the cumulative validated-evidence dossier; make the replacement organizing argument, comparison logic, limitations, and section purposes explicit.

Write feedback/outline-revision.md with the exact action-plan findings addressed, the structural change, and any remaining evidence limitation. Do not draft chapters, alter figures, fabricate sources, or turn an unresolved empirical question into a result. The following scripts re-audit the outline before downstream evidence allocation.

Treat outline.json target_words as a section contract. Measure the chapter set against the project total and expand every materially short section with evidence-backed analysis, comparisons, and limitations until it approaches its allocation. Do not add filler, unsupported claims, or a revision log to reader-facing prose.

Repair every cited factual claim flagged by the evidence audit. Replace generic [source:<source-id>] markers with exact chunk ids from the matching evidence packet, for example [source:<source-id>:p12].
Before finalizing a chapter, make every [source:<source-id>:pN] marker resolve to a source in the current evidence packet and bibliography; remove or rewrite any claim whose marker cannot resolve.
Remove or explicitly qualify claims with no packet-backed evidence. Never preserve a citation merely because its metadata exists.

When feedback/user-feedback.md is present, implement its relevant requests without violating the evidence and citation requirements; describe what changed or could not safely change in reviews/revision-report.md.
Refresh paper/abstract.md when the revision materially changes scope, synthesis, or conclusions. Keep it 150--250 words, reader-facing, citation-free, and free of workflow/process language.

Do not add Markdown pipe tables, hand-numbered Table/Figure references, prose pretending to be a diagram, or delivery/placement instructions for an artifact builder. Preserve the artifact builder's labeled tables and rendered figures; revise the surrounding explanation instead.

Use reviews/artifact-plan.json when it selects a formalization. Decide the exact notation and wording from the cited evidence, define every symbol nearby, and omit the formula if the evidence cannot support a useful formalization. Never fabricate an equation, theorem, or experimental result.

instructions: Write the requested operator question from the validated action plan; do not resolve it or change the manuscript.
